_about: PaperFeed config. Keys starting with _ are comments and are ignored.
_keyword_sets: One block per topic you follow. Every field except 'name' is optional, but a set needs at least one of terms / all_of / authors.

keyword_sets._terms: OR'ed together: a paper matching ANY of these is a hit. Searched as exact phrases in title+abstract. A term containing [ ] is passed to PubMed as raw search syntax.
keyword_sets.name: de novo protein design
keyword_sets._all_of: Every term here must ALSO appear. Use it to narrow a noisy set, e.g. terms=[binder] + all_of=[protein].
keyword_sets._authors: Follow specific people. Written as PubMed writes them: surname then initials. Papers by them get a scoring bonus. Note the search APIs are loose - 'Baker D' will also return papers by 'Baker DA' - but only an exact initial match earns the bonus.
keyword_sets._exclude: Drop papers mentioning any of these, for this set only.
keyword_sets._fields: 'title_abstract' (default, less noise) or 'all' (searches everywhere, including MeSH and full text).
keyword_sets._journals: allow = ONLY these journals. deny = never these. Matched as substrings, so 'Nature' covers 'Nature Methods'.
keyword_sets._sources: Override the global sources for this set only, e.g. {"pubmed": false} to make it preprints-only.
keyword_sets._min_score: Override the global ranking.min_score for this set. Useful for a broad term: a title match is worth 4, so min_score 4 means the paper must be ABOUT this, not merely mention it. Hidden papers are reported and not marked as seen.

_ranking: How papers are ordered. A title match is weighted above two abstract mentions on purpose - the title is what a paper is ABOUT. recency_bonus is deliberately small: inside a 14-day window almost everything is recent, so it is a tiebreaker, not a driver. Set enabled=false to go back to plain date order. min_score hides weak matches (try 2 or 3).
_mute: Applies to every keyword set. Useful for an ambiguous word: 'binder' matches battery-electrode papers, so muting 'cathode' cleans that up. Muted papers are NOT remembered, so removing a mute brings them back.
_collect: The collector makes your library grow on its own. Every run, papers scoring at least min_score are saved automatically, up to max_per_run. Papers you click Save on are marked 'you'; these are marked 'auto', so you can always tell them apart. Turn it off and the library only grows when you click.
_ai: OPTIONAL and off by default. Everything else in PaperFeed - including every dashboard and chart - works with no key at all. The key is read from an environment variable, exactly like the email password: export PAPERFEED_AI_KEY='...' in your shell. It is never stored in this file and never typed into a web page.
_ai_provider: 'anthropic' for the Claude API, or 'openai' for OpenAI and anything that speaks its chat-completions API - Groq, DeepSeek, Together, OpenRouter, LM Studio, Ollama. For those, also set base_url, e.g. 'https://api.groq.com/openai/v1' or 'http://localhost:11434/v1' for a local model.

ai._interests: Free text. The more specific, the better the triage.

_trends: OPTIONAL. Every interval_days, re-queries the last few months and writes a themed briefing. Uses the same provider and key as 'ai', with its own model.
_interval_days: Minimum days between digests. The scheduler wakes the script daily; it exits quietly until this many days have passed.
_lookback_days: How far back each run searches. Keep comfortably larger than interval_days.
_max_per_set: Cap on papers fetched per keyword set per source.
_contact_email: NCBI asks that automated tools identify themselves. Sent as a User-Agent header only.
_email: Set enabled to true once your digests look right. The password is NEVER stored here: set the environment variable named in password_env. For Gmail, use an app password.

email._send_when_empty: Email you even when there is nothing new. Off by default; the digest file is written either way.
